edits.before: Q-shield trades on his last-hits — the empowered auto walk-away is sneakily one of the better level-1 trades mid.
edits.after: Windwall answers your poke and his passive shield eats the rest — he can step to you level 1 while you have only Q-auto.

edits.after: Skill

edits.before: E online: the laser farms AND pokes in one cast. Aim it through minions into his chest on every wave contact.
edits.after: E is online but a 4s Wind Wall deletes it — poke only when the wall is down, farm when it is up; even on wall-reading.

edits.after: Skill

edits.before: Full kit: W zones his aggression and the E-Q-auto trade pattern is fully armed. Stack your first augment quietly.
edits.after: Full kit, but the lane still runs on Windwall timing: W his dash lane, trade in the wall's downtime, farm the rest.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — laser every wave contact and bank Manaflow. Each augment makes the same spells quietly crueler.
edits.after: Clean trades come down to the wall: it is 25s at rank 1 against your 12s E — one baited Windwall buys two free lasers.

edits.before: Yasuo
edits.after: Skill

edits.before: Chaos Storm online — your all-in answer and teamfight entry. In lane it's the kill: W-E-R on anyone who oversteps.
edits.after: At 6 he cannot ult you solo — no knockup in your kit to feed Last Breath — so the all-in stays even; fear ganks, not him.

edits.before: Yasuo
edits.after: Skill

edits.before: Luden's spike: the laser chunks a third bar and the storm executes the remainder. Force extended rotations.
edits.after: Both spike on first item: his dash tempo against your Luden's poke stays a duel decided by Windwall reads.

edits.before: Yasuo
edits.after: Viktor

edits.before: Evolved late-game Viktor is a zone the enemy can't enter: W the choke, E the clump, and steer R through the retreat.
edits.after: Two-plus items you out-scale hard: W roots his dash, evolved E out-DPSes him, and Wind Wall cannot block the storm zone.

edits.before: - Yasuo Wind Wall: matchup-defining — Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. It governs your forward steps. - W Gravity Field spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Yasuo Wind Wall: 25s at rank 1, 17s at max, and it blocks projectiles for only 4s — wait it out, then punish; its downtime is your whole lane. - His R is 70/50/30s but needs a knockup he can't self-supply. - Your W is 17s at rank 1 — save it for his dash.

edits.before: E through the wave into his chest, Q-shield the response, empowered-auto, and walk — a full trade where his answer hit a shield.
edits.after: Feint with Q or an auto first — the wall lasts 4s on a 25s cooldown, so one baited cast buys you two free Hextech Rays.

edits.before: Casting E at melee-adjacent range against a loaded engage — Viktor's cast times are an assassin's favorite metronome.
edits.after: Gravity Field placed pre-emptively on his dash path stops the engage; dropped after he is on you, it stops nothing.

edits.before: Yasuo wins by landing Wind Wall, denying your pattern, and cashing the all-in before your pattern matures.
edits.after: Yasuo wins by walling your laser, dashing the wave with Sweeping Blade, and cashing a gank-fed Last Breath all-in.

edits.before: Yasuo is at his most annoying here: his Windwall (W) eats your Death Ray and Siphon Power's empowered auto, so a good Yasuo negates your poke and dashes through minions with Sweeping Blade (E) to trade. Bait or wait out Windwall's long cooldown before committing your Death Ray.
edits.after: Yasuo is at his most annoying here: his Windwall (W) eats your Hextech Ray and Siphon Power's empowered auto, so a good Yasuo negates your poke and dashes through minions with Sweeping Blade (E) to trade. Bait or wait out Windwall's 25-second cooldown before committing your ray.

edits.before: You out-scale hard into two-plus items: evolved Death Ray plus Chaos Storm out-DPS him, Gravity Field roots him through his dashes, and once he burns Windwall you delete him from range while your frontline denies his gap-close.
edits.after: You out-scale hard into two-plus items: evolved Hextech Ray plus Chaos Storm out-DPS him, Gravity Field roots him through his dashes, and once he burns Windwall you delete him from range while your frontline denies his gap-close.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 give Yasuo the edge because Windwall shuts off your primary poke and his passive shield plus mobility let him step up and trade into your autos. Don't waste Death Ray into an obvious Windwall — farm cleanly and make him use it defensively first. Keep the wave neutral so his Sweeping Blade dashes don't hand him a free engage angle through your minions.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 give Yasuo the edge because Windwall shuts off your primary poke and his passive shield plus mobility let him step up and trade into your autos. Don't waste Hextech Ray into an obvious Windwall — farm cleanly and make him use it defensively first. Keep the wave neutral so his Sweeping Blade dashes don't hand him a free engage angle through your minions.

edits.before: Through levels 3-6 the lane is skill-based: it revolves entirely around his Windwall timing. When it's up, you can't poke and should just farm; when it's down, Death Ray and your empowered auto punish him hard. He can't ult you solo without a knockup, so his kill pressure comes from ganks — ward your flanks and hold Gravity Field to root him if he dashes in. Thin the caster wave so he can't dash-engage for free.
edits.after: Through levels 3-6 the lane is skill-based: it revolves entirely around his Windwall timing. When it's up, you can't poke and should just farm; when it's down, Hextech Ray and your empowered auto punish him hard. He can't ult you solo without a knockup, so his kill pressure comes from ganks — ward your flanks and hold Gravity Field to root him if he dashes in. Thin the caster wave so he can't dash-engage for free.

edits.before: Into first item the fight stays a skill duel around his Windwall and E-dash tempo, but from two-plus items you take over decisively. Evolved Death Ray and Chaos Storm out-DPS him, Gravity Field roots him mid-dash, and once his Windwall is down you blow him up before he closes. In teamfights sit behind your frontline, zone his engage, and let your scaling and range end the matchup he can't reach into.
